name: joystick_deflection_maximum
label: Joystick sensitivity
description: How far the stick has to move for a full signal, also called full deflection. Lower is more sensitive, because a smaller push does the same thing.
source: QMP-4 QuadStick.py slider_UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT (10..50) and calculate_joystick_preferences; qsflash.py defaults '25'

name: joystick_deflection_minimum
label: Joystick center dead zone
description: How far the stick has to move before it counts. Larger is less sensitive near the centre, which stops a resting stick drifting.
source: QMP-4 QuadStick.py slider_NEUTRAL (0..20) and its tooltip; qsflash.py defaults '8'. Firmware 2373 Preferences.h:97 also defaults to 8, and DataFlow.c:997 is where 0 becomes 129 raw counts, overriding Configuration.c:376.

name: deflection_multiplier_up
label: Up deflection multiplier
description: Brings up level with the other directions. Larger is more sensitive going up.
source: QMP-4 QuadStick.py calculate_joystick_preferences computes max*100/slider, so it has no fixed range; qsflash.py defaults '140'

name: deflection_multiplier_down
label: Down deflection multiplier
description: Brings down level with the other directions. Larger is more sensitive going down.
source: QMP-4 QuadStick.py calculate_joystick_preferences computes max*100/slider, so it has no fixed range; qsflash.py defaults '130'

name: deflection_multiplier_left
label: Left deflection multiplier
description: Brings left level with the other directions. Larger is more sensitive going left.
source: QMP-4 QuadStick.py calculate_joystick_preferences computes max*100/slider, so it has no fixed range; qsflash.py defaults '100'

name: deflection_multiplier_right
label: Right deflection multiplier
description: Brings right level with the other directions. Larger is more sensitive going right.
source: QMP-4 QuadStick.py calculate_joystick_preferences computes max*100/slider, so it has no fixed range; qsflash.py defaults '100'

name: joystick_D_Pad_inner
label: Inner D-Pad ring
description: Where the inner D-Pad ring starts, out from the centre. It waits a moment first, so you can pass through it.
source: QMP-4 QuadStick.py slider_D_Pad_inner_ring (10..100) and its tooltip; qsflash.py defaults '25'. Firmware 2373 Configuration.c:367-372 converts it with (value * 1023) / 100, so it is a percent of full deflection from the center, and takes half of it as the release threshold. Preferences.h:101 also defaults to 25.

name: joystick_D_Pad_outer
label: Outer D-Pad ring
description: Where the outer D-Pad ring starts, out from the centre. Past this line the direction fires at once.
source: QMP-4 QuadStick.py slider_D_Pad_outer_ring (10..100) and its tooltip; qsflash.py defaults '80'. Firmware 2373 Configuration.c:367-372 converts it with (value * 1023) / 100, so it is a percent of full deflection from the center. The device's own default is 65 (Preferences.h:102), which is what it uses when a file leaves this out; 80 is what QMP-4 writes.

name: joystick_dead_zone_shape
label: Circular dead zone
description: Makes the centre dead zone round instead of square, so it feels the same in every direction.
source: QMP-4 QuadStick.py checkbox_circular_deadzone writes '1' or '0'; qsflash.py defaults '1'

name: anti_dead_zone
label: Anti dead zone
description: Adds a fixed push to every stick reading, along the way the stick is pointing, to get past a dead zone the game adds of its own. Zero is off.
source: firmware 2373 preference_keywords.h ANTI_DEAD_ZONE, read in DataFlow.c:1187 when it is above zero. Preferences.h:104 defaults to 0. Configuration.c:653-681 sends every preference except the two bluetooth keyword tables and bluetooth_remote_address through atoi, so the value is a whole number. No source states a range, so none is claimed here.

name: enable_auto_zero
label: Auto zero the sensors
description: Your QuadStick ignores this and forces it back to off, so nothing changes either way.

Configuration.c:469 sets it to 0 after the preferences file and the workbook Preferences segment and before the backup copy is taken, and the two reads in DataFlow.c, near :1061 and :1286, are commented out. QMP-4 has no control for it; qsflash.py also defaults '0'.

name: sip_puff_threshold_soft
label: Soft sip/puff threshold

source: QMP-4 QuadStick.py slider_SP_low (5..100) and its tooltip; qsflash.py defaults '8'

name: sip_puff_threshold
label: Normal sip/puff threshold
description: Pressure where a normal sip or puff counts. QMP calls this the hard threshold, but it is what the ordinary sip and puff controls use. Raise it if soft sips keep firing the normal one.
source: QMP-4 QuadStick.py slider_SP_high (10..100) and its tooltip; qsflash.py defaults '40'

name: sip_puff_delay_soft
label: Soft sip/puff delay
description: How long a soft sip or puff waits before it counts. Longer ignores a breath you did not mean.
source: QMP-4 QuadStick.py spin_ctrl_SP_low_delay (min 100, max 3000) and its tooltip; qsflash.py defaults '1300'

name: sip_puff_delay_hard
label: Hard sip/puff delay
description: How long a sip or puff is held before it counts as a long one. On the side tube that is how long you sip to switch game files. The clock starts at the normal threshold, and 0 fires at once.
source: firmware 2373 preference_keywords.h SIP_PUFF_DELAY_HARD, so a mode row can set it. Preferences.h:96 defaults to 2000 ms, and DataFlow.c:349-352 counts from the moment state 2 is reached. The 1000..3000 bounds are QMP-4 QuadStick.py spin_ctrl_SP_high_delay; qsflash.py writes '2400'. Firmware 1476 had no such keyword. DataFlow.c:1313 is the file switching path: right_sip_long needs enable_select_files and the side tube held to state 3, which is this delay.

name: sip_puff_maximum

name: sip_threshold_soft
label: Soft sip threshold
description: Soft threshold for sips only. Leave it at 0 to use the shared soft threshold.
source: QuadStick Google Group, Fred Davison, 2026-08-09, announcing the firmware that splits sip from puff: six new preferences, all default 0, 0 means the matching sip_puff_* setting is in effect. Percent and the default are his; the 0..100 bounds are the unit's own scale. Firmware 2373 preference_keywords.h carries all six and DataFlow.c:290-317 confirms both halves of that: each one is used only when it is not zero, and it scales with the same (value * range) / 100 expression as the combined setting, so the percent means the same thing. Firmware 1476 predates them.

name: bluetooth_device_mode
label: Bluetooth device mode
description: What the QuadStick pretends to be over Bluetooth.
source: firmware 2373 preference_keywords.h bluetooth_device_mode_keywords, the same seven tokens as firmware 1476; QMP-4 QuadStick.py choice_BT_device_mode has them too; qsflash.py defaults 'none'

name: bluetooth_authentication_mode
label: Bluetooth authentication mode
description: How much pairing the QuadStick asks for. Sent to the radio as its SA setting, so it only matters while Bluetooth is on.
source: QMP-4 QuadStick.py choice_BT_auth_mode offers 0, 1, 2 and 4, and its qsflash.py writes '4'. Firmware 2373 Preferences.h:113 defaults to 2, where firmware 1476 Preferences.h:94 defaulted to 4, so the device's own default changed. It is sent to the radio as the SA command in Bluetooth.c:267. The four meanings are Table 2-3 of the Roving Networks Bluetooth Data Module Command Reference (RN-BT-DATA-UG v1.0r), which covers the RN-42: 0 open with no encryption, 1 SSP keyboard I/O, 2 SSP just works, 4 legacy pin code. 3 is not documented, which is why it is not offered. The radio's own default is 1.
optionLabels: Open, no pairing check and nothing encrypted
Confirm the pairing on the other device
PIN code, typed on the other device

name: bluetooth_connection_mode

Configuration.c:653-681 sends every preference except the two bluetooth keyword tables and bluetooth_remote_address through atoi, so the value is a whole number. Joystick.c:344 only compares it to 1.

name: bluetooth_throttle

Configuration.c:653-681 sends every preference except the two bluetooth keyword tables and bluetooth_remote_address through atoi, so the value is a whole number. No source states a range, so none is claimed here.

name: enable_select_files

name: enable_usb_a_host
label: USB-A host mode
description: Newer QuadSticks only. Lets a controller plugged into the USB-A port feed the USB 1 and USB 2 inputs, unless USB-A device mode is on.
source: firmware 2373 preference_keywords.h ENABLE_USB_A_HOST; Preferences.h:135 defaults to 1. JoystickHost.c:590 is the only read: the host is de-enumerated when enable_usb_a_device is set or this one is clear. Firmware 1476 has no such keyword, though QMP-4 QuadStick.py already wrote the name.

name: enable_DS3_emulation
label: USB emulation mode
description: Which controller the QuadStick pretends to be. The console has to know the one you pick.
risk: A mode marked no drive hides the QuadStick's files from your computer until you set it back. The numbers also mean something different on older QuadSticks.
source: firmware 2373 preference_keywords.h maps it to USB_EMULATION_MODE; Descriptors.c:1292 switches on all eight values, DescriptorsDS4.c:803 and :807 tell 6 (no USB drive) from 7 (straight DS4 wireless), and Joystick.c and DataFlow.c switch on the same numbers. Which modes carry a USB drive is read off the configuration descriptors: PS3_t (mode 0), X360CE_t (2), X360_t (3) and CM_t (4 on a computer) each declare an MS_Interface, while DS3_t (1), NS_t (5), Mode6_t (6) and PS4_t (7) do not. Firmware 1476 Descriptors.c:1523 had 5 as PC only, no joystick. Preferences.h:138 defaults to 0. QMP-4 QuadStick.py checkbox_ps4_boot_mode treats it as a checkbox.

name: titan_two
label: Titan Two adapter
description: Newer QuadSticks only. Tells the QuadStick it reaches a PS4 through a Titan Two. Turn it on only if you use one.
source: firmware 2373 preference_keywords.h TITAN_TWO; Preferences.h:146 defaults to 0. JoystickHost.c:570 skips the DS4 authentication state machine when it is set, and Joystick.c:862 and DataFlow.c:2842 both zero the PS4 reset timer. The firmware's own comment at Joystick.c:862 says a T2 makes the QuadStick think it is directly connected to a PS4 when it is not, so that reset is never needed.

name: enable_usb_a_device
label: USB-A device mode
description: Which USB socket the QuadStick appears on. Zero is its own port; above zero is the USB-A socket, and that also turns off USB-A host mode.
risk: Picks which USB port the QuadStick appears on, and it beats USB-A host mode. A wrong value can leave the QuadStick unseen by your console or computer. Change it only on advice from QuadStick support.
source: firmware 2373 preference_keywords.h ENABLE_USB_A_DEVICE, passed to USB_Init and USB_Connect in Joystick.c:599 and :630 and Configuration.c:354-357, and checked first in JoystickHost.c:590. Preferences.h:134 defaults to 0. QMP-4 QuadStick.py writes the separate enable_usb_a_host instead. Configuration.c:653-681 sends every preference except the two bluetooth keyword tables and bluetooth_remote_address through atoi, so the value is a whole number. No source states a range, so none is claimed here.

name: enable_usb_comm
label: Voice commands over USB
description: Lets voice commands arrive over the USB cable.
source: QMP-4 QuadStick.py checkbox_enable_usb_comm writes '1' or '0'; qsflash.py defaults '0'

name: usb_1_multiplier_up

label: USB 2 dead zone
description: Newer QuadSticks only, and your QuadStick ignores it anyway: both sticks on the USB-A port use the USB 1 dead zone.
source: firmware 2373 preference_keywords.h USB_2_DEAD_ZONE; Preferences.h:133 defaults to 20. That line, the Preferences.h:60 enum entry, the keyword table and the Configuration.c:153 default table are the only four places the name appears in the firmware tree, so nothing reads it.

name: watchdog_disable
label: Disable the watchdog
description: Was meant to stop the QuadStick restarting itself when it locks up. Your QuadStick ignores it.
risk: The watchdog restarts your QuadStick if it stops answering. Nothing reads this setting, so today it does nothing.
source: QMP-4 qsflash.py defaults '0'; firmware 2373 preference_keywords.h DISABLE_WATCHDOG, with the two minute watchdog set up in Joystick.c:569-573. Preferences.h:111 defaults to 0. The keyword table, the enum, the default macro and the Configuration.c:131 default table are the only places the name appears.

name: debug
label: Debug output level
description: Turns the QuadStick's console output on when it is above zero.
source: firmware 2373 preference_keywords.h DEBUG_VERBOSITY, read in Configuration.c:375. Preferences.h:119 defaults to 1. Configuration.c:653-681 sends every preference except the two bluetooth keyword tables and bluetooth_remote_address through atoi, so the value is a whole number. No source states a range, so none is claimed here.
